answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (tier party_statement). It relays a quote from Sharon AI's CEO and describes Firmus's DSX AI factory plans as stated by NVIDIA. The article is NVIDIA's own account; no independent source for these claims was supplied.
answer.note: Material claim: NVIDIA says it is introducing a new business model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, using a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Per NVIDIA, NVIDIA would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This supports a conditional read that NVIDIA is shifting part of its compute economics toward revenue-share participation in partner AI cloud capacity, with credit support extended to partners. The source is a stated model and intent, not a reported result: it gives no revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, contract count, signed volumes, or revenue timing. Firmus's Batam campus (expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) is a partner's developer expectation relayed by NVIDIA, so it supports supply-side demand for NVIDIA GPUs in that project only if built as planned. Sharon AI's CEO quote shows a stated collaboration, not volumes. Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI are described as showing where demand is heading, not as named partners in this model. Counterexample check: all quoted facts could hold while NVIDIA earns little from this model, if partner capacity is slow to build or the revenue share and credit support are small; so NVDA revenue impact remains a hypothesis that needs the missing financial terms.
limitations: No financial terms are disclosed: the revenue-share rate, the scope and size of credit support, and how product and cloud revenue would be recognized are all unstated.

Whether any AI cloud has signed an agreement under this model is not established by the source; the named companies are described as collaborators or as examples of demand, not as confirmed counterparties with volumes.
The Firmus campus scale (360 MW, up to 170,000 GPUs) is an expected figure from a partner, with no stated completion date, funding status, or NVIDIA purchase commitment.
The source is NVIDIA's own promotional post, so it does not independently confirm adoption, demand or economics.
Timing of any revenue or cash effect for NVIDIA is not disclosed, so the model cannot be placed in a specific fiscal period from this source.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's latest 10-Q/10-K and earnings-call transcripts for disclosure of this model, revenue-share arrangements, guarantees or credit support extended to AI clouds, and any related contract liabilities or receivables.

Search for announcements by Sharon AI and Firmus of financing, construction milestones and GPU delivery schedules for the stated campuses, to see whether the expected scale is backed by committed funding.
Check whether Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI have announced agreements with NVIDIA or with the named AI clouds under this model, separating confirmed contracts from demand commentary.
Look for any independent coverage or analyst estimates of the economic size of the revenue-share and credit-support model to test the stated earnings stream.
